column1: # Where a hit would be visible for a root outside `rules:`, which of the
# stand's own invariants that probe has to withdraw, and — where the canonical
# write cannot hit anything — what a hit actually looks like.
# The default observable is `findings`: the digest of the reported violation
# population. It is wrong for every root whose effect is not a finding, and a
# stand that used it everywhere would call those roots NOT OBSERVABLE and call
# `withdraws` names an invariant of the stand that stands in the same place as
# the probed door — a probe taken beside its own shadow measures the shadow,
# which is the lesson the input-door stand paid for. `target` is the positional
# `src` argument: it shadows both the `paths` key and the `paths` CLI door.
# `hit` exists because a probe without a hit is not a probe. The canonical list
# write `[7331]` names nothing in the fixture, so on a root whose values are
# paths, namespaces or rule names it changes nothing and the sensitivity probe
# goes blind — and the row would then read NOT OBSERVABLE for a reason that
# belongs to the stand. These hits are the control values of
#   findings  the sorted (file,line,channel,severity,message) digest plus the count
#   stdout    the shape of what was printed, with digits normalized
#   cachedir  which cache directories exist after the run
#   logfile   the resolved value echoed into the debug log
